- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, especially in early horizon.
- Model frequently overshoots after recent price spikes (e.g., +5–10% above true), especially if sentiment is positive — apply downward correction in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative mid-horizon, model may lag in adjusting downward — apply early correction to avoid prolonged overestimation.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show strong upward trend, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate in high-sentiment periods; consider 20-day rolling average for smoother correction.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” (no sentiment), model tends to err on the low side — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate.
